answer: The network admits agents using a system where 1,000 unique credential nullifiers define the absolute limit of identity, preventing sybil clusters. A verifier checks each request against a persistent global record; should an identity relic surface in multiple indices, it triggers an immediate prune. An honest participant pays once to register, while an attacker seeking 1,000 identities must independently forge distinct proof-of-work paths to bypass the nullifier checks. The system acts as a lantern for auditability, where collisions lead to permanent revocation without any refundable stake.
